questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to structure a DP solution for scheduling with deadlines and selection limits, including schedule reconstruction.

## Key Concepts
- Weighted interval scheduling with job count constraint
- DP with backtracking for schedule reconstruction
- Time/space optimization and tie handling

## Code Example
```python
# DP[i][j]: max profit using first i jobs with j chosen
# p(i): rightmost index < i compatible with job i
for i in 1..n:
  for j in 1..K:
    DP[i][j] = max(DP[i-1][j], DP[p(i)][j-1] + profit[i])
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you optimize to O(n K) space?
- What if jobs have release times?
- How to handle parallel workers?

Tests advanced tree DP combining child subproblems with path count constraints, requiring careful handling of edge-disjoint root-to-leaf paths.

## Key Concepts
- Tree DP with knapsack merging across children
- Edge-disjoint path packing constraints
- Reconstruction via predecessor pointers
- Complexity trade-offs (NK² vs NK optimizations)

## Implementation Notes
- Post-order DFS for bottom-up computation
- Store predecessor information for path reconstruction
- Knapsack merging ensures optimal path selection

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you optimize from O(NK²) to O(NK)?
